## Summary

## User journey

Andrés buys a salsa ticket or Camila confirms a viewing with a trip selected → payment/schedule truth is saved → itinerary row appears once → webhook replay does not duplicate it.

## Frontend work

* Booking confirmation card links to trip workspace itinerary tab.
* Show paid/scheduled item in itinerary after sync.
* Capture screenshot/evidence for ticket and viewing paths.

## Backend / Supabase work

* Extend event order/showing sync from `event_orders` and `showings` into `trip_items`.
* Upsert idempotently on `unique_trip_item (trip_id, item_type, source_id)`.
* Extend `item_type` via data-027 for `event`/`showing` as needed.
* Snapshot event/showing title, venue/address, lat/lng, and `start_at`.
* Store metadata: `order_id`, `stripe_payment_intent`, `webhook_event_id`, `sync_source`, `synced_at`.
* Prefer edge function proximity to payment truth.
* If trip item insert fails, return 500 so Stripe retries; do not cache webhook success until side effects are committed or explicitly queued for TRIP-013 repair.

## Agent / CopilotKit / Mastra work

* CopilotKit can render confirmation link/card.
* Mastra can observe/display state but must not set paid status.
* Gemini must not invent payment status, booking status, trip truth, or itinerary rows.

- [ ] Scheduled viewing appears after confirm flow.
- [ ] Webhook replay does not duplicate rows.
- [ ] SQL select and screenshot evidence attached.
- [ ] Failure-mode test proves trip_items insert error is not cached as webhook success.

## Do not do

* Do not add a durable queue table for MVP; TRIP-013 adds lightweight repair first.
* Do not let LLM set payment status.

## Summary

Prove that Trips data cannot leak across users. This is the task that makes sure Camila cannot see, update, delete, join against, or infer another traveler’s trips or saved itinerary items.

## User journey

User A creates a trip and saves private rentals or events → User B logs in with a separate JWT → User B cannot read, mutate, delete, join, count, or infer User A’s trip data from app routes, direct Supabase calls, or edge/runtime paths.

## Frontend work

* Add/extend Playwright multi-user fixtures where useful.
* Cover `/trips`, trip workspace routes, saved collections, itinerary, add-to-trip, conflict UI, and any API-backed buttons that mutate trip data.
* Confirm UI does not reveal unauthorized counts, titles, map pins, conflict badges, or empty-state differences that leak private data.
* Mobile behavior must preserve the same isolation; no cached cards from another user after account swap.

## Backend / Supabase work

* Verify RLS for `trips`, `trip_items`, saved-link tables used by Trips, conflict records, and any supporting views/RPCs.
* Test SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, JOIN, count inference, and nested relation leakage.
* Confirm service role is only used in approved server-only paths and never in browser/client code.
* Add Supabase JWT swap tests or SQL-level proof scripts.
* Validate edge functions and `/api/copilotkit` cannot bypass user ownership checks.

## Agent / CopilotKit / Mastra work

* Ensure CopilotKit readable state and HITL cards only receive the authenticated user’s trip rows.
* Gemini must not expose, summarize, infer, or fabricate another user’s trip, booking, payment, or saved-item truth.
* Agent tools must require user/session context and must fail closed when auth is missing.

## Tech stack

Next.js 16, React 19, Tailwind 4, shadcn/ui, CopilotKit 1.55.2, Mastra, Gemini, Supabase, Google Maps, Places API, Stripe where relevant, Playwright.

## Dependencies

* Internal: TRIP-001, TRIP-003, TRIP-007, TRIP-009

## Acceptance criteria

* User A cannot SELECT, UPDATE, DELETE, JOIN, or infer User B’s trips or trip items.
* Edge/runtime paths enforce the same ownership boundary as direct Supabase calls.
* Service-role usage is proven absent from browser/client surfaces.
* Multi-user proof is committed as evidence.
* Any discovered policy gaps are fixed before TRIP-011 and TRIP-012 pass.

## Do not do

* Do not rely only on happy-path UI tests.
* Do not treat service-role success as user-auth proof.
* Do not mark complete without negative tests.
* Do not weaken RLS for agent convenience.

## Summary

Add a lightweight repair path for the case where Stripe confirms a booking but the Trips itinerary item is missing. This protects Andrés or Miguel from paying for a ticket and then seeing an empty trip timeline.

## User journey

Andrés buys a ticket through Stripe → the webhook should create the related `trip_items` row → if that insert fails or times out, the reconciliation worker finds the paid booking later → the trip itinerary is repaired without manual support intervention.

## Frontend work

* No primary new screen for MVP.
* Trips itinerary and workspace must show repaired booking items once the worker backfills them.
* Admin/support surfaces may later expose repair results, but this task should keep the MVP UI impact limited to restored trip items.
* Any user-visible recovered item must avoid duplicate itinerary entries.

## Backend / Supabase work

* Implement `repair_missing_trip_items()` as a lightweight reconciliation routine.
* Run it every 15 minutes via `pg_cron` or the project-approved scheduled mechanism.
* Compare paid/confirmed booking truth against `trip_items`.
* Insert missing trip items idempotently.
* Add indexes or uniqueness constraints needed to prevent duplicate repairs.
* Record repair attempts and failures in structured logs or a minimal audit table/path used by TRIP-017.
* Validate tenant/user ownership before writing repaired rows.

## Agent / CopilotKit / Mastra work

* No agent should create booking/payment/trip truth from model output.
* Gemini may explain that a booking is being synced, but it must not invent payment status, booking status, Stripe status, or itinerary truth.
* If a CopilotKit card references a repaired item, it must read from Supabase state only.

## Tech stack

Next.js 16, React 19, Tailwind 4, shadcn/ui, CopilotKit 1.55.2, Mastra, Gemini, Supabase, Google Maps, Places API, Stripe where relevant, Playwright.

## Dependencies

* Internal: TRIP-010
* External: data-028

## Acceptance criteria

* Paid bookings missing `trip_items` are detected and repaired.
* Repair is idempotent and safe to run repeatedly.
* Duplicate itinerary rows cannot be produced by repeated worker runs.
* Failures are visible in logs/evidence for Patricia or Sofía to investigate.
* Local proof includes a simulated missing-trip-item case and a successful repair.

## Do not do

* Do not introduce a heavyweight queue system for the MVP.
* Do not make Gemini or Mastra the source of booking truth.
* Do not mark bookings paid without Stripe-confirmed evidence.
* Do not silently swallow repair failures.
